text_blocks.snippet: Treatment for atrial fibrillation (AFib) focuses on controlling heart rate, restoring a regular heart rhythm, and preventing stroke. Treatment options include medications, lifestyle changes, and procedures like cardioversion or catheter ablation. The best approach depends on individual factors like the severity of symptoms, overall health, and the type of AFib.
snippet_highlighted_words: medications, lifestyle changes, and procedures like cardioversion or catheter ablation

list.title: Rate control:
list.snippet: Medications like beta-blockers (e.g., metoprolol, atenolol) and calcium channel blockers (e.g., diltiazem) are used to slow down a rapid heart rate during AFib episodes.

list.title: Rhythm control:
list.snippet: Antiarrhythmic drugs (e.g., amiodarone, dronedarone) can help restore and maintain a normal heart rhythm.
